independence_note: Separate implementation and separate cache. Where worker-099 re-fetched sampled locators and judged excerpt grounding, this task runs a 97-row census of declared identifier -> bibliographic identity and never reads the ledger's own verdict column as evidence for its own check. 12 of 97 rows had prior independent coverage bound to this hash; the census adds the other 85.
method: Census, not sample: every row of the frozen CSV, every distinct DOI (86) and every distinct arXiv id (58). Crossref /works/<doi> for each DOI; DataCite /dois/<doi> fallback where Crossref is a 404; batched arXiv Atom API for ids. Each resolved record compared to the row's declared title at preregistered thresholds (Jaccard >= 0.60 or difflib ratio >= 0.80), dual-identifier rows compared DOI-record vs arXiv-record, and authors checked at surname-token level. 114 cached registry bodies, each re-hashable; report is byte-identical between fetch and offline replay.

findings.finding: The identifier layer of the frozen L1 ledger is clean across the whole population: 0/97 rows resolve to a work whose title contradicts the declared title, and 59/59 dual-identifier rows resolve both channels title-compatibly. 46 of the 59 carry an explicit registry cross-link (arXiv id in Crossref or DOI in arXiv); the other 13 agree by title at the frozen thresholds.
findings.falsifier: Show one cached DOI body and cached arXiv body for a row reported IDENTITY_MATCH that belong to different works, or one row reported clean whose cached record contradicts the declared authors at surname level.

findings.finding: 26 of 92 DOI-bearing rows are invisible to a Crossref-only checker. 25 are arXiv-issued 10.48550/arXiv.* DOIs that are registered with DataCite and return HTTP 404 from api.crossref.org; the 26th is a university thesis DOI (SRC-007, 10.25365/thesis.76304). All 26 resolve at DataCite. A first pass that queried Crossref only produced 31 spurious FETCH_FAILED rows (26 DOI + 5 legacy arXiv-id parse); both causes were diagnosed and fixed, and neither is a defect in the ledger.
findings.falsifier: Query api.crossref.org/works/10.48550/arxiv.2204.09891 and show HTTP 200, or query api.datacite.org/dois/10.48550/arxiv.2204.09891 and show HTTP 404.

findings.finding: 18/97 rows carry an arXiv-preprint year earlier than the declared journal year (offsets 2-6 years; e.g. SRC-002 arXiv 2019 declared 2023, SRC-093 arXiv 2005 declared 2009). After correcting the author metric from exact-name to surname-token matching, zero author-overlap flags remain. The offsets are the expected preprint->publication pattern and are recorded as flags, not normalized away.
findings.falsifier: Show that the declared year for one of the 18 rows is the arXiv submission year rather than a later journal year in the same row's venue field.

findings.finding: 10 duplicate-identifier groups (6 DOI, 4 arXiv) cite one work from two citation ids: SRC-021/SRC-056, SRC-033/SRC-088, SRC-023/SRC-055, SRC-060/SRC-072, SRC-059/SRC-071, SRC-002/SRC-068 (DOI); SRC-066/SRC-089, SRC-057/SRC-086, SRC-002/SRC-068, SRC-024/SRC-087 (arXiv). In every group the two declared titles are title-compatible at the frozen thresholds; the strings differ only by trailing provenance annotations such as '(Crossref record)', '(arXiv ...)', or '(OpenAlex abstract reconstruction)'. The useful result is that the same work is sometimes bound through its arXiv id and sometimes through its journal DOI, so a dedup rule must key on the resolved record, not the identifier string. This is a ledger-owner question, not an identity defect.
findings.falsifier: Show that one of the paired citation ids carries a declared title incompatible with its partner at the frozen thresholds for a reason other than a trailing provenance annotation, or a different used_by_theorems binding that makes the pair non-duplicate.

findings.finding: Threshold-boundary observation, not a mismatch: SRC-057 and SRC-086 are the same paper (arXiv 1702.05715 / Annals 190(1) 1-111) but their declared titles differ by the subtitle '. The interior of the black hole region', giving Jaccard 0.583 and ratio below 0.80. Both rows resolve to compatible records through their own identifiers, so no row verdict is affected; this pair is only visible as an artefact of my declared-title comparison and shows the frozen 0.60/0.80 thresholds are sensitive on long titles with a dropped subtitle. Recorded because a stricter threshold would have produced a false mismatch here.
findings.falsifier: Show that SRC-057 and SRC-086 resolve to different works rather than the same arXiv id and its published version.

findings.finding: SRC-011 declares the 1969 Penrose paper and its DOI (10.1023/A:1016578408204) resolves to the 2002 'Golden Oldie' reprint in General Relativity and Gravitation: title carries a '"Golden Oldie": ' prefix and the Crossref year is 2002. The row's venue field already records the reprint, title compatibility is 0.78 Jaccard / 0.89 ratio, and the author resolves at surname level, so the row is a legitimate reprint binding rather than a mismatch.
findings.falsifier: Show a distinct DOI for the 1969 original that the row should have used, or show the row's venue field does not record the 2002 reprint.

findings.finding: SRC-020 and SRC-044 carry neither a DOI nor an arXiv id; each is an INSPIRE record only. Both were fetched live this pass and resolve to the declared title (literature/1767922 -> 200, literature/2743272 -> 200). They are correctly classed NO_IDENTIFIER rather than failures; a future locator policy should state whether an INSPIRE record id is an acceptable sole record locator.
findings.falsifier: Fetch the two INSPIRE record ids and show either returns non-200 or a title contradicting the declared title.

non_claims: Does not claim the ledger's evidence excerpts support the theorems it cites; worker-099's SRC-025 FAIL and the L0 content verdicts own that question.

Does not claim the 27 literal-ellipsis exact_locator rows from W025-L1-LOCATOR-ADJ-01 are record locators; that finding stands separately, and this audit shows the alternative anchors/identifiers resolve.
Does not set, promote, or pre-judge any gate verdict, validation_status, or node status.
Does not edit the ledger, the map, research_map/formulation_taxonomy.yaml, or any frozen artifact.
